sentences.ko: 욕을 먹어도 일단 이름 알려지면 이득이야.
sentences.text: There is no such thing as bad press.

alts.text: Any press is good press.
Even negative publicity ends up being beneficial.

sentences.note: **no such thing as** 는 '그런 건 세상에 없다'고 딱 잘라 말할 때 씁니다. **bad press** 는 언론이나 사람들 입에 나쁘게 오르내리는 것을 말합니다. 좋든 나쁘든 화제가 되면 손해는 아니라고 할 때 하는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 난 그냥 있을래. 지난번에 스키 타러 갔을 때 리프트에서 내리는 게 너무 무서웠거든.
sentences.text: I'm going to stay cuz the last time I went skiing, I was too afraid to jump off the chairlift.

alts.text: Nah, I'm staying. Last time I went skiing, I was too scared to get off the lift.
Actually, I will stay here, because the last time I went skiing, I was too afraid to get off the chairlift.

sentences.note: **the last time I went** 는 '지난번에 ~했을 때'라는 뜻이라, 예전 경험을 들어 핑계를 댈 때 그대로 씁니다. **too afraid to** 는 '너무 무서워서 ~를 못 했다'는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 잠깐 나랑 이쪽으로 좀 와 볼래?
sentences.text: Will you come here with me for a minute?

alts.text: Got a sec? Come here.
Could you come with me for a moment, please?

sentences.note: 사람들 앞에서 따로 할 말이 있어서 한 사람만 불러낼 때 하는 말입니다. **for a minute** 는 정말 1분이 아니라 '잠깐'이라는 뜻이고, **Will you** 로 물으면 부드럽게 부탁하는 말이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: OH, you should have told me that before.

alts.text: Ugh, why didn't you say so earlier?
It would have been better if you had told me that earlier.

sentences.note: **should have told me** 는 '진작 말해 줬어야지'라는 뜻으로, 일이 다 끝난 다음에 그 얘기를 듣고 아쉬워하거나 투덜댈 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: Uh, do you guys have plans for the weekend?

alts.text: Any plans this weekend, guys?
Does everyone have any plans for the weekend?

sentences.note: 주말에 뭐 하냐고 물을 때는 단수 plan이 아니라 **have plans** 라고 복수로 씁니다. 여러 사람에게 한꺼번에 물을 때는 **you guys** 를 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니 그냥, 우리가 아는 여자 중에 포커 칠 줄 아는 사람이 마침 없어서 그래.
sentences.text: Yeah, we just don't happen to know any women that know how to play poker.

alts.text: Thing is, none of the girls we know play poker.
Unfortunately, we do not happen to know any women who play poker.

sentences.note: **don't happen to know**는 '일부러 그런 게 아니라 어쩌다 보니 모른다'는 뜻이에요. 왜 안 했냐고 물을 때 변명하듯 답하는 자리에서 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이제야 너희가 무슨 말 했던 건지 알겠더라.
sentences.text: I finally started to see what you guys were talking about.

alts.text: Now I get what you guys meant.
I have finally begun to understand what you were all saying.

sentences.note: 여기서 **see**는 '보다'가 아니라 '이해하다'예요. 친구들 말을 처음엔 못 믿다가 나중에 직접 겪고 "아, 이제 알겠다" 할 때 **see what you guys were talking about**을 통째로 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: I'll bet it went better than you think.

alts.text: Bet it went way better than you think.
I am sure it went better than you believe.

sentences.note: **I'll bet**은 '장담하는데, 분명히'라는 뜻이에요. 면접이나 발표를 망친 것 같다고 걱정하는 친구를 달랠 때 딱 맞아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그래서, 그 여자 진짜 또 만날 거야?
sentences.text: So, are you actually going to see her again?

alts.text: You really gonna see her again?
Do you actually intend to see her again?

sentences.note: **see her again**은 데이트 상대를 '다시 만나다'예요. **actually**를 넣으면 '정말로? 의외네'라는 느낌이 붙어서, 소개팅 다녀온 친구한테 캐물을 때 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 남의 인생을 그렇게 좌지우지할 수 있는 건 좀 부담스러워.
sentences.text: I'm I'm not comfortable having that kind of power and control over someone's life.

alts.text: I don't want that much say over someone's life.
I do not feel comfortable having that degree of power over another person's life.

sentences.note: **not comfortable having**은 '~하는 게 부담스럽다, 내키지 않다'예요. 중요한 결정을 대신 내려 달라는 부탁을 정중하게 사양할 때 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends
